summary.description: Lead is a bluish-white, very dense, soft, highly malleable and ductile metal.
emission_sources: Burning of fossil fuels in power stations
Historical use in petrol, paints, and plumbing (now largely phased out)
environmental_impact: Lead is a cumulative poison affecting the central nervous system
Causes developmental harm to unborn children and brain development in children
Toxic to plants and animals at high exposure, persists in soils and sediments
Potential carcinogen and harmful to male reproductive system

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Lead exposure is highly toxic to human health, particularly affecting brain development in children, the central nervous system, and reproductive health.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Lead contaminates soils and sediments and can become more soluble in acidic water, threatening clean water sources.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Historical and ongoing releases from industry and fossil fuel burning highlight the need for responsible management of lead use and emissions.
